cards.title: Engage a QC agent for initial manufacturing orders
cards.claim: Using a QC agent for first-time (and even second or third-time) manufacturing orders helps ensure product quality by checking against the Tech pack, weighing, measuring, and verifying Pantone colors.
cards.action: Engage a QC agent to go to the factory and inspect the product. Alibaba offers an inbuilt QC function; alternatively, use a third-party like SGS (which is expensive but also does compliance).
applies_when: second or third time using a manufacturer
unknowns: Cost of QC agent (SGS noted as expensive)
evidence_quotes: I highly highly recommend that every single uh first time that you use a manufacturer even the second or third time that you're using a QC agent to go check the product
you can just say hey send a QC agent out to this order or you can use any of the other ones like SGS it's quite expensive and big but they do compliance as well

cards.title: Use a critical path to manage production timelines
cards.claim: A critical path method—defining every step, sequencing events, estimating duration, assigning dates, setting reminders, and monitoring daily—helps avoid delays such as missing Christmas trade.
cards.action: Create a critical path by defining all process steps, sequencing them in order, estimating time for each (e.g., sample shipping from China might take 5 days via DHL), assigning dates, setting reminders for overdue tasks, monitoring daily, and assigning roles. Use project management tools like Monday.com, Notion, or Excel.
unknowns: Which project management tool is best (speaker uses Monday.com but says impartial)

cards.title: Forecast inventory using in-stock periods and appropriate time comparisons
cards.claim: Forecasting aims to determine reorder date and quantity; avoid using out-of-stock periods for extrapolation, and for businesses less than 1-2 years old with rapid growth, use month-on-month comparisons.
cards.action: When forecasting, select periods when product was in stock (e.g., use 15 in-stock days rather than 30 days with 15 out-of-stock days). For businesses less than a year or less than 2 years old with quick growth, look at month-on-month sales. Use tools like Inventory Planner or Excel for visibility.
